featured.title: Pre-RFC: `pub(api)` visibility, and static enforcement of crate-internal API boundaries
featured.summary:
It shouldn't block pub(api) because, as mentioned, it would become a weak keyword. The set of possible first tokens in a pub(E) context I believe are self, super, and in otherwise. If that is the case, then introducing api as another should not be ambiguous.
While pub can be used within a module, the rustc lints documentation suggests that the only reason this isn't a default warning is that it would break too much code right now, and may change. See my reply to @robofinch about…
featured.reason: New visibility RFC impacts Rust API design
featured.suggestedSummary: A new pre-RFC discusses the introduction of `pub(api)` visibility in Rust, aimed at statically enforcing crate-internal API boundaries. This proposal suggests using `pub(api)` as a weak keyword to manage visibility, allowing developers to define APIs that are public within a crate but not exposed externally. This can significantly improve encapsulation and modularity in large Rust projects, providing a more flexible and powerful way to manage API boundaries compared to existing mechanisms like `pub(in path)`.

featured.title: Narwhal v0.6.0 – message broker for edge apps, now with channel persistence
featured.summary:
hi again! i'm back with a new release of Narwhal, the lightweight message broker for edge apps i shared a while ago. the headline change in v0.6.0 is channel persistence: channels and their message history can now be durably stored on disk, so subscribers can replay missed messages after reconnecting. also swapped the async runtime from monoio to compio (still io_uring on Linux), and added first-class Prometheus metrics.
